title: Power Cut

items.label: Dark Study Room
items.description: A student leans over a book in a room whose light has gone out.
items.visual_focus: a student bent over an open book below a switched-off lamp
items.local_cue: a Bangladeshi student's notebook and locally typical small apartment furnishings

items.label: Hot Room
items.description: A person fans themself beside a motionless ceiling fan.
items.visual_focus: a person fanning their face beneath a still ceiling fan
items.local_cue: a Rajshahi apartment ceiling fan and an open summer window with metal grille

items.label: Phone Flashlight
items.description: A student aims a phone light at a notebook as the battery icon glows low.
items.visual_focus: a phone flashlight beam falling directly on a student's notebook
items.local_cue: a Bangladeshi student using a phone torch at a compact apartment study table

items.label: Generator Fumes
items.description: A shopkeeper starts a small generator while a passerby covers their nose.
items.visual_focus: a generator exhaust pipe and a nearby person's covered nose
items.local_cue: a small petrol generator at a ground-floor Bangladeshi shop entrance

items.label: Dead Router
items.description: A worker tries to reconnect a laptop beside an unlit router.
items.visual_focus: an unlit router beside a laptop showing a broken-connection symbol
items.local_cue: a compact router and laptop at a Rajshahi apartment study table

items.label: Limited Charging
items.description: Several people wait to charge devices at one small battery backup.
items.visual_focus: several charging cables competing for one small backup battery
items.local_cue: several Bangladeshi students and a small backup battery on an apartment table

questions: Which two scenes make studying hardest?
When did a power cut last change your plans in Rajshahi?
Should a shared backup power point serve students or shops first? Why?
Why might a shop use a smoky generator despite the cost?
If one building offers free charging, what new problem might appear?
You have 150,000 BDT and 30 days. What one backup-power idea would your grant test?

grant.pilot_scope: Pilot backup light and charging for one shared study area.

evidence.basis: supplied brief plus Rajshahi student reporting
